tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: This repository serves as the packaging and CI backbone for OxiGuitar, a guitar tablature viewer. It does not contain the application source code itself; instead, it manages the distribution pipeline: building plugin packages, signing apt/dnf repositories, and publishing them to GitHub Pages for end-user installation. README.md provides the entry point with installation instructions and an overview of the project's purpose.

tour.title: Contribution Guidelines
tour.description: Before diving into the code, understand the project's development conventions. CONTRIBUTING.md defines the branch and pull request workflow along with Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) sign-off requirements. RELEASING.md covers the GitHub App setup and branch rule configuration needed to trigger automated releases. CLAUDE.md provides standing rules for working with the project's AI assistant, including branch and commit conventions.

tour.title: CI/CD Workflows
tour.description: The project's automation lives in six GitHub Actions workflows that form the CI/CD backbone. ci.yml enforces quality gates (formatting, linting, tests, license checks, and DCO validation) on every merge to develop and main. The plugin-release workflow is the most connected node with 4 incoming edges: it builds .oxp packages across Linux, Windows, and macOS, producing deb, rpm, zip, and Inno Setup installers. plugin-publish.yml triggers repository updates, while site.yml builds and publishes the apt/dnf repository index to GitHub Pages.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers to define when they run, 'jobs' for parallelism, and 'steps' for sequential execution. Matrix builds test across multiple OS and architecture combinations. The repository_dispatch event enables cross-repository workflow triggering, which plugin-publish.yml uses to notify oxiguitar-packages when a new plugin release is ready.

tour.title: Release Pipeline
tour.description: The release flow connects multiple workflows and scripts into a coherent pipeline. release.yml triggers plugin-release.yml, which in turn triggers plugin-publish.yml, which ultimately triggers site.yml. The scripts layer provides the supporting tools: fetch-packages.sh downloads release artifacts, the plugin-package/ subdirectory contains platform-specific builders (deb.sh, rpm.sh, windows.sh), and bump.sh handles version bumping across Cargo.toml, manifests, and CHANGELOG files.

tour.title: Testing & Quality
tour.description: Quality assurance is woven into both the CI pipeline and the manual testing scripts. check-dco.sh validates commit sign-offs, make-test-packages.sh creates local .deb and .rpm packages for verification, test-install.sh confirms packages install correctly on target systems, and test-bump.sh exercises the version bump process safely. The trial plugin-release-try.yml workflow provides a sandbox to test the release pipeline without publishing.

tour.title: Plugin Source Code
tour.description: The trial plugin directory contains two Rust crates that serve as the only real application code in this repository. Each plugin follows a consistent pattern: a Cargo.toml defines the crate metadata and dependencies, a manifest.json declares the plugin interface (id, name, version, effects), and lib.rs implements the Trial class with start, effect, and prepare methods plus a Pass struct with a process method. The build-oxp.sh script packages these crates into .oxp plugin archives.
tour.languageLesson: Rust plugin crates use the oxiguitar-plugin trait interface, implementing Trial and Pass types that the host application loads dynamically. The workspace Cargo.toml shares package metadata (version, authors, license) across crates via [workspace.package], reducing duplication. cargo-deny (deny.toml) enforces license compliance and bans unsafe dependencies at build time.

tour.title: Configuration & Site
tour.description: The configuration layer defines project-wide standards: clippy.toml and rustfmt.toml enforce Rust code style, deny.toml manages license compliance and dependency security, and dependabot.yml automates dependency updates. The site layer contains the single-page GitHub Pages site (index.html) that hosts the apt/dnf repository installation instructions, built by build-site.sh and deployed by site.yml. The winget.md documentation and make-winget-manifests.sh script handle Windows Package Manager submissions as a separate distribution channel.
